correctness.rationale: For every fixed \(r\ge2\), the exact local generating function gives \(F_r=\mathbf{1}*h_r\) with \(h_r\ge0\). The quotient of \(H_r(s)\) by \(K((r+1)s)\) has a Dirichlet series absolutely convergent to the left of \(\theta=1/(r+1)\). The classical Selberg–Delange theorem gives the squarefree-weight mean, yielding \(N_r(x)\sim A_r x^\theta/\sqrt{\log x}\). Summation by parts, regular variation and the fractional-part identity for \(\zeta(s)\) give a discrepancy coefficient \(-\zeta(\theta)A_r\), strictly positive. Exact rational checks independently verify local identities and finite convolutions for four power orders through integer index \(3000\), but are not used to assert an infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: The February 2026 motivating paper treats this identical composition but obtains only the leading-order term with \(O_r(x/\log x)\) error for the critical weight \(k=2\); the present formula determines a sharp, noninteger power-log deficit with explicit coefficient. A 2022 article treats the uncomposed weight, not the minimal-power composition. Implicit precedence via broad Tauberian results remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: A more general Tauberian or regularly-varying divisor-sum theorem may implicitly encompass the exact secondary term without its particular arithmetic notation.

value.rationale: The \(k=2\) normalization is arithmetically natural: division by the number of unitary divisors. It makes the leading singularity a simple pole yet leaves a positive sublinear discrepancy. The theorem computes its nonzero sign, optimal power-log order and Euler-product constant for each fixed \(r\ge2\), improving the published \(O_r(x/\log x)\) remainder by a power of \(x\). This gives a motivated exact secondary law, not a numerical or purely cosmetic refinement.
